why: The rename map sent Root to ZqOld and RootNew to ZqNew, which reverses the order of the two getters (Root < RootNew, ZqNew < ZqOld). Rule P4 names a PAR-weak law and orders its claim's two sides by the getters' names, so no derivation can satisfy the test under that map: the prereg instrument itself (tests_m3/_i24x.py::expected, run on the renamed copy exactly as the test builds it) derives L_par_weak_HdrBytes_ZqNew_HdrBytes_ZqOld_v2 where the renamed original law id is L_par_weak_HdrBytes_ZqOld_HdrBytes_ZqNew_v2, and every other law agrees. The one change: RootNew now maps to ZqOldNew, an order-preserving renaming (Root < RootNew and ZqOld < ZqOldNew); under it the instrument's two derivations agree law for law and statement for statement. The other renamings, the fixture, the derivation and every assertion are unchanged; the test still renames the Solidity functions (enc_x, load_x), the record fields and the Go methods (Root, RootNew, makeV2).
